lines.say: 3 a.m. Nobody's awake, and your app just emailed ten thousand people their receipts.
lines.show: 3 a.m. Nobody's awake, and your app just emailed *10,000 people* their receipts.

lines.say: Nobody. A cron job did. It's a scheduled task, like a repeating alarm for your server.
lines.show: Nobody. A [cron job] did. It's a scheduled task, like a *repeating alarm* for your server.

lines.say: You set the timing once: every day at three a.m.
lines.show: You set the timing once: *every day at 3 a.m.*

lines.say: When the alarm rings, your server runs the code that emails the receipts.
lines.show: When the alarm rings, your server [runs the code] that *emails the receipts.*

lines.say: One catch. Set up that same task on two servers, and both alarms ring. People could get two receipts. So keep the schedule in one place.
lines.show: One catch. Set up that same task on *two servers,* and both alarms ring. People could get [two receipts.] So keep the schedule *in one place.*

lines.say: Linux has cron built in, and Kubernetes has CronJobs.
lines.show: *Linux* has cron built in, and *Kubernetes* has CronJobs.
